name: ioperm
synopsis: int ioperm(unsigned long from, unsigned long num, int turn_on);
description: ioperm sets the I/O port access permission bits for the calling thread for a specified range of ports. It enables or disables permissions based on the turn_on parameter, requiring privileges if enabling. This call is primarily for the i386 architecture and may not be supported on others.

parameters.name: num
parameters.description: Number of ports to set permissions for

parameters.name: turn_on
parameters.description: Nonzero to enable permissions, zero to disable

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Invalid values for from or num.
This call is not supported (on PowerPC).
The calling thread has insufficient privilege.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.8, only the first 1023 I/O ports could be specified; before Linux 2.4, permissions were not inherited by child processes via fork; this call is mainly for i386 and may fail on other architectures.
versions: Linux 2.4 and later for permission inheritance; Linux 2.6.8 and later for full port support up to 65,536 ports.
